name: Muse Mesh 5: tooling for the text-mesh track
description: Builds the tools around the text-mesh pipeline described in docs/08-mesh-track.md: augmentation, a text-to-GLB exporter, multi-view renders, a caption script, a training-set builder with leak-free splits, and an eval report. Every tool is verified offline with tiny fixture meshes.

userStories.title: mesh_augment: rotate, mirror and recolour text meshes
userStories.description: As the dataset builder, I want label-preserving augmentations of a text mesh so that 120 real objects become several hundred distinct training examples.
steps: Create tests/fixtures/mesh/ with 3 tiny valid meshes as JSONL lines (id, name, caption, text) in tests/fixtures/mesh/objects.jsonl: a cube, a pyramid and an L-shape, each with one `c` colour group, longest side spanning 0..63, standing on y=0.

Create scripts/mesh_augment.py importing parse_text from glb_to_text and validate from mesh_validate. Provide pure functions `rotate_y(text, quarter_turns)`, `mirror_x(text)`, `recolour(text, mapping_or_hue_shift)` that return new mesh text. After a rotation or mirror re-centre on x and z and keep y=0 and the longest side at 63, using the same integer rounding as glb_to_text.to_text.

Add `augment(row, rng, n)` returning up to n variants (dedup by text, never equal to the original) and a CLI: `--in data/mesh/objects.jsonl --out data/mesh/augmented.jsonl --per-object 4 --seed 1`. Each output row keeps `source_id`, gets a new `id`, and records which transforms were applied.

Write tests/py/test_mesh_augment.py: every variant of every fixture passes validate(); four quarter turns return the original vertex set; mirror twice returns the original; recolour changes only `c` lines; the CLI is deterministic for a fixed seed.
acceptanceCriteria: rotate_y, mirror_x, recolour and augment exist and are covered by at least 6 tests
Every augmented fixture mesh passes mesh_validate.validate
Running the CLI twice with the same --seed writes byte-identical files
Augmented rows carry source_id so a later split can keep copies of one object together
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: mesh_to_glb: write a text mesh as a GLB file
userStories.description: As a user of the trained model, I want its text output saved as a GLB so it opens in Blender, Unity and the animation-timeline model3d layer.
steps: Create scripts/mesh_to_glb.py using only numpy and the standard library (no new dependency). `text_to_glb(text) -> bytes` builds a binary glTF 2.0 file: one mesh, one primitive per `c` colour group, shared POSITION accessor with float32 positions mapped from 0..63 to a 1-unit cube (x,z centred, y from 0), uint16 or uint32 indices, one PBR material per colour with baseColorFactor in linear space, correct accessor min/max, 4-byte aligned buffer views, JSON and BIN chunks padded per the GLB spec.
Add a CLI: `--in mesh.txt --out model.glb`, and `--jsonl data/mesh/objects.jsonl --out-dir data/mesh/glb --limit N` for batches.

Write tests/py/test_mesh_to_glb.py: for each fixture the output starts with the glTF magic, the header length equals the file length, the JSON chunk parses, accessor counts match the text; then read the file back with scripts/glb_to_text.read_glb and collect, run to_text, and assert the vertex count and triangle count match the original (round trip).

Add a Chromium check in tests/py (skipped with a clear message if Chromium cannot launch) or a node test under tests/js that loads one produced GLB with the local three@0.160.0 GLTFLoader and asserts it has at least one mesh.
acceptanceCriteria: text_to_glb output round-trips through glb_to_text.collect and to_text with equal triangle counts for all fixtures
The GLB header, chunk lengths and 4-byte alignment follow the glTF 2.0 spec (asserted in tests)
Colour groups become separate primitives with their own materials
No dependency beyond numpy is added to requirements.txt
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

userStories.title: mesh_views: render each mesh from four angles
userStories.description: As the caption pipeline, I want four PNG views of every mesh so a vision-capable model can describe what the object is.
steps: Create scripts/mesh_views.mjs by reusing the parsing and lighting approach in scripts/preview_mesh.mjs (do not edit that file). For each row of a JSONL, render 4 views (front, right, back, three-quarter above) at 256x256 on a plain background with the local three@0.160.0 and SwiftShader flags, and write data/mesh/views/<id>_<0..3>.png.
Flags: `--in`, `--out-dir`, `--limit`, `--size`, `--concurrency` (default 2). Skip rows whose four files already exist, so a rerun is resumable.

Write tests/js/mesh_views.test.mjs using node:test: render the three fixture meshes into a temp dir, assert 12 PNGs exist, are 256x256, are not a single flat colour, and that the four views of the L-shape differ from each other.
Document usage in docs/08-mesh-track.md under a short 'Views' heading.
acceptanceCriteria: Rendering the fixtures produces 4 PNGs per mesh, each 256x256 and not blank
Views of an asymmetric mesh differ pairwise (compared by pixel difference in the test)
A second run renders nothing and exits 0 because all files exist
scripts/preview_mesh.mjs is unchanged
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

userStories.title: caption_meshes: write captions with a model, mocked in tests
userStories.description: As the dataset builder, I want a resumable script that asks a model to describe each mesh from its views so captions are richer than file names.
steps: Create scripts/caption_meshes.py. For each row of data/mesh/objects.jsonl it builds a prompt from the model name and, when `--views-dir` has the four PNGs, attaches them (base64) in the OpenAI-compatible image message format. Backends: `--ollama-native` (like teacher_generate.py) or an OpenAI-compatible `--base-url` with `--api-key` and `--model`.

Ask for 3 short captions of different lengths (terse, plain, detailed) as JSON lines; parse tolerant of fences and chatter; reject captions that mention a file name, a pack name, or contain the words 'mesh', 'obj', 'vertex'. Write one JSON per object to data/mesh/captions/<id>.json with `id, name, captions, model, ts`, resumable and never saving failed calls.
Provide `merge_captions(objects_path, captions_dir) -> rows` that attaches `captions` to each object, falling back to the name-derived `caption` when no file exists.

Write tests/py/test_caption_meshes.py with a fake backend object (no network): parsing happy path, fenced JSON, chatter around JSON, rejected captions, resume skips existing files, failed call not saved, merge fallback. Text-only mode is the default when no views exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Caption parsing and the banned-word filter are covered by at least 6 tests
A rerun with every caption file present makes zero backend calls (asserted)
No test touches the network; the backend is injected
The script prints how many objects were captioned, skipped and failed, and states 'not run on real data' in the docs rather than inventing results
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: build_mesh_dataset: leak-free prompt/completion JSONL
userStories.description: As the trainer, I want train and validation files where all augmented copies of one object stay on the same side of the split, in the prompt/completion format train_sft.py reads.
steps: Move the SYSTEM string out of scripts/mesh_baseline.py into scripts/mesh_prompt.py (`SYSTEM`) and import it in both places; behaviour of mesh_baseline.py must not change.

Create scripts/build_mesh_dataset.py: inputs `--objects`, optional `--augmented`, optional `--captions-dir`; output `data/mesh/sft/train.jsonl` and `val.jsonl` with `{"prompt": ..., "completion": ...}` where prompt is the SYSTEM text plus the caption and completion is the mesh text. When an object has several captions, emit one example per caption (cap with `--max-captions`).

Split by source object, not by row: `--val-fraction 0.1`, seeded, stratified loosely by pack. Write `data/mesh/sft/split.json` listing which source ids are in val. Re-validate every completion with mesh_validate.validate and drop failures, reporting counts by reason.

Write tests/py/test_build_mesh_dataset.py on the fixtures: no source id appears in both files, every completion validates, the split is deterministic for a seed, captions fan out to several examples, and the prompt contains the SYSTEM text exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria: No source object id appears in both train.jsonl and val.jsonl (asserted, including augmented copies)
Every completion in both files passes mesh_validate.validate
mesh_baseline.py still imports and its SYSTEM text is unchanged (asserted by comparing to a stored hash or literal in a test)
split.json is written and deterministic for a fixed seed
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: eval_mesh: pass rate, failure breakdown and comparison report
userStories.description: As the person presenting the result, I want one command that turns baseline and trained-model runs into a before/after table and a screenshot-ready report.
steps: Create scripts/eval_mesh.py. Input: one or more run folders in the format scripts/mesh_baseline.py writes (one JSON per caption with ok, reason, stats, tokens, secs, plus summary.json). Compute pass rate, failure reasons, median faces of passing meshes, tokens per answer and seconds per mesh.

Support pass@k: when a folder holds several samples per id (files named `<id>__<k>.json`) report the share of ids with at least one passing sample for k=1..max. Single-sample folders report pass@1 only.

Write `--compare a b ...` Markdown output with one row per run and the delta in pass rate against the first run, plus the per-reason table; write it to a file given by `--out` (default stdout). Never invent numbers: an empty folder reports 'no results'.

Write tests/py/test_eval_mesh.py with hand-made run folders under a temp dir: pass rate, reason counts, pass@k with 2 samples per id, comparison deltas, empty folder, a folder with a malformed JSON file (skipped and counted).
acceptanceCriteria: Pass rate, reason counts and pass@k are covered by at least 6 tests using hand-made folders
--compare prints the pass-rate delta against the first run
An empty or missing folder prints 'no results' and exits non-zero without a traceback
docs/08-mesh-track.md gains a short 'Eval' section listing the commands, with 'not measured' wherever real numbers are not yet known
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Tests use tiny hand-written meshes under tests/fixtures/mesh and mocked HTTP. Nothing calls Ollama, Baseten or any remote model. New files only except where a story says otherwise; do not edit the Three.js-code-track scripts.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.
